data.programDescription: Funds awarded to 32 projects as part of Alaska RHTP Year 1 to drive rural health transformation with a focus on care coordination, infrastructure, workforce development, cybersecurity, health IT upgrades, new technologies, and alternative payment model pilots.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Recent Updates: Year 1 Funding Announcements

data.programDescription: Modernizing Behavioral Health Infrastructure to Strengthen Alaska’s Workforce and System of Care — AK Child & Family proposes implementing integrated technology solutions that strengthen behavioral health documentation, care coordination, workforce management, and communication. The project addresses fragmented systems, administrative burden, and workforce capacity challenges that affect service coordination for children, youth, and families served across Alaska, including those from rural and remote communities receiving care through AK Child & Family programs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Behavioral Health Support for Vulnerable Youth — AWARE, in partnership with the City and Borough of Juneau Zach Gordon Youth Center, proposes to increase behavioral health support for vulnerable youth, ages 0-21yrs,  who are utilizing AWARE victim services, Zach Gordon's Shéiyi Xaat Hít Youth Shelter services, or day services at Zach Gordon Youth Center. This project serves youth and families utilizing hub services in Juneau from surrounding towns/villages in northern Southeast Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural and Frontier point-of-are ultrasound Initiative — Alaska Academy of Family Physicians proposes to expand point-of-care ultrasound training and equipment access for healthcare professionals in rural and remote Alaska. The project addresses limited local access to diagnostic imaging, long distances to specialty care, and insufficient opportunities for hands-on ultrasound training in underserved communities by providing hands-on education and point-of-care ultrasound equipment to physicians, advanced practice clinicians, nurses, paramedics, Community Health Aides, and other front line healthcare workers serving rural Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Electronic Medical Record Implementation — Alaska Addiction Rehabilitation Services, Inc. proposes implementing an electronic health record system to improve clinical documentation, care coordination, and data management, addressing the lack of a centralized patient record system for adults receiving substance use disorder treatment from communities across Alaska, including rural and remote areas.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: The Road Home: Intensive Care and Community Integration for Alaskans with Complex Needs — The Alaska Association on Developmental Disabilities proposes to expand Alaska's capacity to support individuals with intensive needs by establishing a new level of care option for Alaskans with intellectual and/or developmental disabilities and other mental health disabilities whose behavior support needs cannot be met in standard community settings. This addresses a long-identified gap in Alaska's continuum of care by creating time-limited step-down settings with dedicated clinical oversight designed to stabilize behavior and support planned transition back to community-based living.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Alaska's Rural Disability Workforce and Support System — Alaska Association on Developmental Disabilities proposes expanding GoodLife Innovation’s evidence-based workforce stabilization, technology advancements, remote support, and education surrounding innovating housing models, including host homes, to strengthen access to consistent services, increase workforce stability, and improve continuity of care for individuals with disabilities and aging adults in rural and remote Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Behavioral Health Workforce Development, Clinical Internship Program — Alaska Behavioral Health proposes expanding a statewide clinical internship program to train master’s-level behavioral health students, addressing Alaska’s shortage of culturally responsive providers across rural, remote, and frontier communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Seeds of Change Model Expansion for Behavioral Health Engagement — Alaska Behavioral Health proposes expanding the Alaska Seeds of Change model to increase behavioral health engagement and reduce treatment dropout among Alaskans with mental health challenges and serious mental illness by creating therapeutic group, activity, and skill-building experiences in a structured hydroponic growing space in Anchorage, serving clients of all ages, including those transitioning to and from rural communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Patient Portal and HIE Integration — Alaska Behavioral Health proposes to integrate its electronic health record with Alaska’s Health Information Exchange and implement a patient portal to improve care coordination and patient access. This project addresses fragmented health systems and limited patient access across rural Alaska by enabling real-time data sharing and empowering patients to manage their care statewide.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Fairbanks Crisis Stabilization Center Development and Implementation — Alaska Behavioral Health will develop and launch a crisis stabilization center in Fairbanks, providing a safe alternative to emergency departments and law enforcement response for behavioral health crises. The project improves access, reduces high-cost utilization, and strengthens coordination across Interior Alaska. All implementation activities will be completed within the performance period ending June 30, 2027.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Rural Routine Outcome Monitoring & Measurement-Informed Care Initiative — The Alaska Behavioral Health Association proposes implementing routine outcome monitoring and measurement-informed care infrastructure with behavioral health providers, addressing the lack of consistent outcome measurement and treatment feedback systems across Alaska’s rural and frontier behavioral health organizations.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Behavioral Health Supervisor Academy Implementation Initiative — The Alaska Behavioral Health Association proposes implementing a statewide behavioral health supervisor academy, addressing limited access to structured supervision training and leadership development opportunities for supervisors serving behavioral health organizations across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Alaska Center for Children and Adults
data.programDescription: Community Pathways — The Alaska Center for Children and Adults (ACCA) proposes to expand screening, care navigation, and partnerships to reach families in its service regions who face barriers to accessing services due to location or ineligibility for existing programs. This will address gaps in access to early developmental, behavioral health, and family support services. The project includes community partnerships and a work-based training program to develop qualified staff.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Alaska Coalition on Housing and Homelessness
data.programDescription: Update of the Alaska Homeless Management Information System for Data Sharing with the Department of Health — The Alaska Coalition on Housing and Homelessness proposes to update the Alaska Homeless Management Information System to improve its ability to securely integrate and exchange data with health systems. Currently the data system is not able to share or compare data with other data systems. The goal is to strengthen care coordination between housing and healthcare services, improve data matching capabilities and support better understanding of health needs among people experiencing homelessness. The coalition serves approximately 15,000 individuals experiencing homelessness statewide every year.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Building healthier communities through containerized aeroponic mini-farms off the road system — Alaska Commercial Company (AC Stores) proposes to grow fresh produce locally and year-round in four of the larger communities that we serve. We intend to use compact indoor growing systems to address the unreliable supply of fresh fruits and vegetables in remote communities across Western, Northern, and Southeast Alaska. All communities in this project are not on the road system.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Eating Disorders Workforce Development and Interdisciplinary Training Infrastructure Initiative — Alaska Eating Disorders Alliance (AKEDA) proposes a 12-month planning and early implementation phase to develop a statewide interdisciplinary workforce training infrastructure for eating disorder identification and treatment, in partnership with UAA College of Health. Activities include a mixed-methods workforce needs assessment, identification of continuing education opportunities, establishment of an interdisciplinary advisory structure, and exploration of a graduate-level training pathway. The initiative addresses a critical statewide gap: Alaska has no dedicated eating disorder care and no coordinated training pathways for an estimated 65,000 Alaskans living with eating disorders.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Alaska’s Eating Disorders Continuum of Care — Alaska Eating Disorders Alliance proposes to strengthen Alaska's eating disorder continuum of care by expanding prevention and provider and parent education, patient navigation, and recovery support statewide. Eating disorders are among the most lethal mental health conditions, yet Alaska lacks the trained workforce, care pathways, and recovery infrastructure needed to identify and treat them. This project will address the most critical gaps and continue to build infrastructure across prevention, treatment, and aftercare for Alaskans statewide.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Essential Obstetric Skill Sustainability: A Rural Alaska Simulation Initiative — Alaska Hospital and Healthcare Association proposes establishing a mobile itinerant clinical training program and distributing localized simulation kits to address the critical gap in emergency obstetric readiness and stabilization across rural healthcare facilities for frontier Alaskan communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Find Your Fit — The Alaska Hospital & Healthcare Association (AHHA) requests funding to expand and enhance “Find Your Fit”, a comprehensive career platform and targeted recruitment campaign. Developed in partnership with Alaska’s 24 hospitals, 20 skilled nursing facilities, and tribal health system, this coordinated statewide initiative builds a robust "grow our own" pipeline to address critical shortages by connecting high schoolers, adult learners, and direct care professionals to certification pathways and rural training opportunities, career pathways, and employment opportunities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Development of an Alaska Nursing Workforce Center — AHHA proposes to incubate the Alaska Nursing Workforce Center, which would serve as Alaska's first dedicated hub for nursing workforce data, research, and strategic planning—addressing a gap as one of only four states without such a center. Year 1 activities focus on finalizing a three-year strategic plan, strengthening governance and operational infrastructure, and beginning statewide nursing workforce data collection. The long-term goal is for the Center to transition to an independent 501(c)(3) organization that informs statewide recruitment, retention, and nursing education policy.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Health Clinic (RHC) Transformation & Financial Sustainability Project — AHHA proposes Strategic, Financial, and Operational Assessments (SFOAs) for three independent Critical Access Hospitals—Petersburg Medical Center, Cordova Community Medical Center, and South Peninsula Hospital—plus implementation assistance for Rural Health Clinic (RHC) designation for those four facilities. The assessments will evaluate revenue cycle efficiency, Medicare cost report optimization, service line performance, and swing bed growth, with a median expectation of approximately $2.4M in identified improvement opportunity per hospital. The project targets financially fragile rural hospitals that serve as sole providers for their communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Healthcare Workforce Housing Catalyst — Alaska Housing Finance Corporation proposes offering flexible housing assistance for up to 150 healthcare workers in 5 communities with 10,000 or fewer people that are located off the road system.  This assistance will be for healthcare workers new to the community and can be used for up to $1,000 / month rent or homeowner assistance for 12 months as a continually employed healthcare worker.  The assistance can flex from rental to homeowner assistance during the service period and will help recruit and retain new healthcare workers struggling with housing availability and costs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska 100% Communities: Community-Led Systems for Access to Care — Alaska Impact Alliance proposes to implement the '100% Communities' model in three communities—Central Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Peninsula, and Ketchikan—creating cross-sector action teams, shared referral pathways, and community navigator roles to address fragmented service access. The project will conduct a Community Access Assessment, map existing services into the 907 Navigation platform, and establish inter-agency coordination infrastructure designed to outlast the grant period. The model focuses on social determinants of health barriers—transportation, childcare, housing, and service navigation—that prevent rural residents from accessing available care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: 907 Navigation App Expansion Project — The Alaska Impact Alliance will expand the 907 Navigation platform to connect residents with health care, social services, public benefits, local resources, and timely community information, addressing gaps in service navigation, referral coordination, and access to reliable information for rural, remote, and frontier communities across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Friendship Circle All-Inclusive Early Childhood Play Center & Programming — The Alaska Jewish Campus proposes developing an inclusive, indoor early-childhood play center, enhancing the existing Outdoor Play Center and  providing year-round warm, safe, accessible opportunities for play, movement, and social connection, addressing the shortage of inclusive recreation and developmental support opportunities for young children with disabilities and their families. Open to the public, free of charge, the Play Center serves children from Anchorage, Mat-Su and visitors from across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Health Education and Support Services Program including a Pre-apprenticeship Healthcare Training Academy — Alaska Literacy Program proposes to expand its Health Education and Supportive Services program through pre-apprenticeship healthcare training and community health education to address critical healthcare workforce shortages and low health literacy across Alaska. The project will create structured career pathways into entry-level healthcare roles through training and workplace readiness certifications, and train multilingual community members to help adults and families navigate health systems; serving rural, remote, and underserved Alaskans facing barriers to education and care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Remote Monitoring and Pre-Employment Screening for Alaska Maritime Crews — Alaska Maritime Physicians proposes to deploy continuous wearable vital-sign monitoring across approximately 425 commercial vessels statewide and launch an observational pre-employment screening pilot for high-risk maritime crew. The project addresses the gap in real-time physiologic oversight for mariners operating in remote Alaska waters, where undetected clinical deterioration drives avoidable medical evacuations and strains rural coastal facilities. The program serves Alaska's commercial maritime workforce across all coastal and frontier regions.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: ANTHC-UW Emergency Medicine Residency and Faculty Strengthening Program — The Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC) proposes to expand its existing partnership with the University of Washington (UW) to establish a statewide Emergency Medicine (EM) Residency Elective and Faculty Exchange Program in Alaska. In Alaska’s rural communities, hospital emergency departments are often staffed by physicians without residency training in EM, leading to disparities in patient health outcomes. This initiative will strengthen the healthcare workforce by improving access to emergency medical care for patients and supporting the training and retention of EM physicians.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Statewide Tribal Pharmacy Development — Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium proposes expanding access to medications and pharmacist-led care through medication access and optimization services, pharmacy automation, modernized pharmacy systems, and statewide pharmacy workforce development to address barriers to medication access, care coordination, and pharmacy service capacity for Alaska Native people and rural communities across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Compatibility Assessment for Wireless Wearable Technology for Continuous Vital Sign Monitoring — The Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC) proposes to evaluate wireless wearable technology for continuous patient vital-sign monitoring and to pilot it on a single inpatient unit, addressing the gap in continuous monitoring at rural facilities where intermittent manual vital-sign checks can leave early patient deterioration undetected, for Alaska Native and rural residents served across the Alaska Tribal Health System.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Capacity and Bed Management to Improve Access to Care, Patient Flow, and Care Coordination — Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium (ANTHC) proposes a health system-wide bed capacity management improvement initiative that integrates operational process redesign and staff training enabled by the Cerner Bed Capacity Management Module to improve patient flow, resource utilization, and care coordination, addressing capacity constraints and delays that affect rural and underserved populations traveling from remote Alaska communities to access specialized healthcare services and higher levels of care unavailable locally.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Community Health Led Medicaid Value Initiative — The Community Health Led Value Initiative will transform community health centers into a strong primary care–led value platform for Alaska Medicaid. By combining team-based care, coordinated outreach, expanded access, and shared data infrastructure, the initiative will reduce avoidable utilization, improve chronic disease outcomes, and create an accountable, sustainable model of care for Medicaid patients throughout Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural FQHC Transformation for Alaska Medicare Beneficiaries — The Alaska Primary Care Association, on behalf of Resolute Health Alliance of Alaska LLC, proposes to implement a Medicare Shared Savings Program value-based care model across four Federally Qualified Health Centers serving rural and underserved Alaskans. This project builds on initial work started in January 2026, and accelerates the transition from volume-based to value-based care by building the clinical workflows, workforce capacity, and population health data systems needed to improve care quality and long-term financial sustainability for rural Alaska's Medicare beneficiaries.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Alaska Psychiatric Institute, Department of Family & Community Services
data.programDescription: Alaska Psychiatric Institute Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Improvements — Alaska Psychiatric Insitute (API) proposes to upgrade its EMR which will strengthen secure exchange of health information with partner providers and improve continuity of care for individuals receiving services at API, including those returning to rural and underserved communities throughout Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Statewide Deployment of Clinical AI Decision Support Network Across Alaska Hospitals — Alaska Stroke Coalition proposes a statewide AI imaging network across 21 acute care hospitals that pairs broad multi-pathology triage with advanced stroke imaging, so every site — urban or rural — receives the same rapid interpretation support for time-critical findings: stroke, hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, aortic and spinal injury. Utilizing two complementary, cloud-based platforms that run on existing PACS without new imaging hardware — diagnostic breadth everywhere, plus the stroke depth needed to treat and transfer faster, while surfacing incidental findings for earlier intervention.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: APIA Facility Renovation and Community Wellness Enhancement (Anchorage and Unalaska) — Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association proposes to establish and expand primary care, behavioral health, and wellness services by improving clinical and community health spaces for Alaska Native people in remote Aleutian and Pribilof Islands communities, including Unalaska and Anchorage. The project will renovate and reconfigure office layouts to create private, functional, and secure spaces for health and social services. This will improve delivery of primary care coordination, behavioral health, victim services, elder case management, and veteran suicide prevention services.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Rural Care Coordination through Expansion of Community Health Worker and Social Work Services — APIA proposes to expand care coordination by adding one medical social worker and two community health workers to its primary care team. This addresses critical workforce shortages and gaps in patient support services for people living in the remote communities of Atka, Nikolski, St. George, and Unalaska. This addresses critical workforce shortages and gaps in patient support services for people living in the remote communities within APIA's Primary Care Services service area (Atka, Nikolski, St. George and Unalaska).

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening APIA Rural Diagnostic Capacity through Laboratory Expansion — The Aleutian Pribilof Islands Association (APIA) proposes to expand laboratory capability at all four Primary Care Services clinics in the remote Aleutian and Pribilof Islands. This project will install a Piccolo Chemistry Analyzer at Nikolski Health Center and deploy troponin-capable point-of-care diagnostic systems at all sites, including the Oonalaska Wellness Center hub. These upgrades will enable timely onsite testing, reduce delays in critical care (especially cardiac events), minimize costly patient travel and medevacs, and improve health outcomes for rural Unangax communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: All Alaska Pediatric Partnership: Readiness for a Coordinated Pediatric System of Care — All Alaska Pediatric Partnership (A2P2) proposes an administrative readiness project to strengthen organizational capacity for implementing a multi-phase expansion of Help Me Grow Alaska's referral pathways and service tracks, in support of a more coordinated statewide pediatric system of care. Two contractors will support project design and implementation planning and organizational/workforce readiness respectively. This readiness investment is designed to position A2P2 to successfully implement a companion DOH-solicited Targeted Innovation proposal.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Statewide Client Management System for ADRD, Care Coordination, and Reimbursement Infrastructure — Alzheimer's Resource of Alaska (ARA) proposes to implement an integrated, statewide client management platform to consolidate ADRD services, Medicaid waiver care coordination, mini-grant administration, and Community Care Hub workflows currently tracked across multiple fragmented tools and paper-based processes. The project will hire a Data Manager, engage a strategic advisory consultant, establish KPIs and data governance structures, and select and begin implementing a unified system that supports billing, referral tracking, and reporting. This infrastructure redesign is intended to strengthen ARA's capacity to deliver coordinated care statewide and support Medicare billing through the Community Care Hub pilot.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Digital Infrastructure and Systems Transformation — Anchorage Neighborhood Health Center proposes to build and implement a modernized technology and clinical infrastructure, expand telehealth and interoperable data systems, and establish workforce support capabilities, addressing outdated infrastructure and fragmented operations for patients in Anchorage and across Alaska, including those in rural and remote communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Builds and implements a modernized technology and clinical infrastructure, expands telehealth and interoperable data systems, and establishes workforce support capabilities, addressing outdated infrastructure and fragmented operations for patients in Anchorage and across rural/remote Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription:
Center for Supporting Healthy Families Project — The Arctic Slope Native Association proposes the expansion of health care services in the Arctic Slope Region through the creation of a single coordinated center for families to access health care
referrals, health education, social services, and other family supports to address specific needs for their children.

This project will address gaps in service delivery where referrals might get stuck or lost between programs, parents complete multiple or duplicate intake/eligibility forms, or people seeking services may discover that they are in the wrong building to access a particular program.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Surgical Suite Renovation — The Arctic Slope Native Association proposes to renovate space at the Samuel Simmonds Memorial Hospital to create a surgical suite in Utqiagvik Alaska. This project provides access to surgical care for approximately 10,000 residents that would otherwise have to leave the community.  Creating this access reduces travel impact on expectant mothers, elderly/medically fragile patients, and improves response times for trauma patients.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Community Alcohol and Other Drug Abuse Health Assessment & Planning — Arctic Slope Native Association (ASNA), in partnership with the North Slope Borough Health and Social Services Department, proposes a $500,000 feasibility study to assess the viability of establishing a sober living environment and detox facility on the North Slope, where 42% of households report being impacted by alcohol or drug use and inpatient AODA treatment currently requires patients to leave Alaska. The study will identify barriers to sustainable AODA services, evaluate operating models, and produce architectural concepts. Findings will be shared regionally and statewide as a potential model for addressing AODA service gaps in rural Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Virtual Intensive Care Unit Project — The Arctic Slope Native Association proposes to address the complete lack of intensive care unit beds in the region by installing technology to create three virtual intensive care rooms at the Samuel Simmonds Memorial Hospital. Upgrading these rooms will allow complex cases to be treated in the region rather than transferring them to Anchorage.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Point of Care Ultrasound & PACS System — Arete Family Care, LLC proposes to acquire a diagnostic ultrasound system and integrated PACS to establish on-site imaging capability at our Anchorage primary care clinic, addressing the lack of accessible, affordable diagnostic imaging for uninsured, underinsured, Medicare, and Tricare patients who face significant delays, transportation barriers, and referral dropout when referred to external facilities for routine abdominal, pelvic, thyroid, and vascular studies.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: I/DD Remote Monitoring Feasibility Study — Assets Inc. proposes a feasibility study to evaluate the potential for remote monitoring of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD) in rural Alaska communities, assessing connectivity, equipment, staffing, and cost-effectiveness as an alternative to urban institutional care. The study will include community interviews in a selected pilot location to gauge user comfort, digital literacy, and training needs, alongside regulatory and vendor evaluation. Results will inform a follow-on pilot project and eventual expansion of telehealth-based in-home support for rural I/DD clients.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bartlett EHR Conversion — Bartlett Regional Hospital (BRH) proposes to upgrade and consolidate its Electronic Health Record (EHR) system by purchasing and implementing an advanced system that will integrate records for all our service lines and clinics, allowing us to deliver secure, efficient, high-quality, data-driven healthcare to Southeast Alaska. Currently, BRH's main hospital, skilled nursing facility, Home Health and Hospice, pediatric clinic and other clinics use separate EHR systems that are not connected and cannot access emerging AI tools and functions.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bartlett Secure Communication Expansion — Bartlett Regional Hospital proposes to expand and enhance the hospital's communication infrastructure by adding modules to our secure communication software that improve patient engagement and functionality for staff in a way that is HIPAA compliant. The enhanced system will allow our patient population of 70,000 Southeast Alaskans to engage with their healthcare in a secure platform integrated with hospital scheduling and care team communications. Consolidating these functions improves reliability, reduces manual outreach burdens, and enhances the speed and safety of clinical decision-making.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Brave Heart Maternity Home - Strengthening Alaska’s Healthy Beginnings — Brave Heart Maternity Home proposes establishing Alaska's first maternal stabilization home to keep pregnant and postpartum mothers and infants safely together. The project addresses the gap in maternity housing and coordinated prenatal, behavioral health, recovery, and parenting support for women in crisis, including those facing homelessness, DV, poverty, substance use, or child welfare involvement in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and surrounding rural communities. Pregnant women experiencing homelessness are an invisible population, untracked until a crisis forces an emergency response.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay: Supporting Communication in Our Villages — Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation (BBAHC) proposes to expand the scope of an existing hospital project, purchasing devices to assist with communication and hearing for our patients in rural villages. Many residents of the Bristol Bay Area have un- or undermanaged hearing loss, which makes it difficult to communicate with caregivers and family members in a clinical setting. BBAHC will provide low cost, high quality, and durable Assistive Listening Devices to village-based clinicians and Community Health Aides to use when interacting with patients in one-on-one settings.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay CHA Recruitment: Adventure, Service and Compassion in the Alaska Frontier — Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation proposes a campaign to recruit and retain Community Health Aides who perform vital health care services in BBAHC village clinics and are key part of our regional health care delivery system in a remote part of Southwest Alaska. The campaign will feature successful CHAs working with patients in the clinic, engaged in cultural activities in the villages and chronicle their journey. Our goal is to promote workforce development through “grow your own” pathways and raise awareness of the need for CHAs, their importance, and impact in people’s lives.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay Home Health — Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation (BBAHC) proposes to hire a consultant to help design policies, procedures, care models, and billing infrastructure for an integrated home health program serving its 28-village region in Bristol Bay. The planning effort will focus on creating a coordinated, billable home care model that utilizes Community Health Aides, nurses, telehealth, and remote monitoring devices to support homebound and chronically ill patients across villages with limited clinic access. The goal is a sustainable, evidence-based home care framework that reduces avoidable hospitalizations and supports patients unable to travel to clinic settings.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay Rural Health Pathways Fellowship — Bristol Bay Foundation proposes the Bristol Bay Rural Health Pathways Fellowship, a cohort-based workforce development program designed to support emerging healthcare professionals in completing their training and building lasting connections to the communities they will serve. The Fellowship addresses the persistent shortage of culturally rooted healthcare providers across Bristol Bay's remote, frontier communities where geographic isolation, high provider turnover, and a long history of externally recruited workforces have left the region chronically underserved.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Supports a cohort-based rural health workforce fellowship for emerging healthcare professionals to address provider shortages in remote Bristol Bay communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Revitalizing Marrulut Eniit Assisted Living (Grandma’s House) for Aging in Place in Bristol Bay — The Bristol Bay Native Association proposes to restore and reopen the Marrulut Eniit Assisted Living Center in Dillingham, Alaska, to address the lack of local assisted living, health care and long-term support services for Elders in the Bristol Bay region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay Prenatal Outreach & Perinatal Support Project — Bristol Bay Native Association proposes building a coordinated, culturally grounded maternal health support system that provides outreach, care coordination, and referral support, addressing gaps in prenatal, postpartum, substance use disorder (SUD), and family support services for Alaska Native families across the Bristol Bay region, including both rural communities and Bristol Bay residents living in Anchorage and the Matanuska-Susitna Valley.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mental Health Supports for Early Childhood — CCS Early Learning will establish a Behavioral Health Associate training hub — using Head Start classrooms as a real-world learning environment — and an early childhood mental health clinic for children ages 0–5. In 2023–24, 44% of CCS-enrolled children qualified based on foster care or homelessness — 7 times the national Head Start average — documenting acute need for expanded behavioral health services in Alaska's Matanuska-Susitna Borough.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bristol Bay Regional Specialty Care Hub Transformation Project — Camai Community Health Center proposes designing a regional specialty care hub to expand local access to visiting specialists, tele-optometry, behavioral health, and victim support services that rural residents of Bristol Bay Borough currently travel great distances to reach or cannot access at all.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: ACCESS (Alaska Collaborative for Clinic-Based Emergent Stabilization Services): Frontier Emergency Stabilization Transformation Project — Cama'i Community Health Center proposes implementing the ACCESS (Alaska Collaborative for Clinic-Based Emergent Stabilization Services) Project, a frontier emergency stabilization demonstration that develops a scalable framework and sustainable reimbursement methodology for independent rural safety-net providers delivering high-acuity emergent stabilization services in remote communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Southeast Alaska Cancer Care Support Network — Cancer Connection will create a Southeast Alaska Cancer Support Network, uniting nonprofit organizations serving rural communities across the region. Network participants will increase knowledge of each organization’s programs, develop strategies to improve patient and provider awareness, and establish a framework to strengthen referrals and access to services. By linking independent programs through shared information, joint initiatives, and healthcare partnerships, the Network will expand access to cancer prevention, treatment, and survivorship support for patients and families.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Project HEARTH: Health & Education Advancement through Rural Telehealth Hubs — Cartwheel proposes, in partnership with the Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation and the Fairbanks and Anchorage school districts, to deliver mental health care via telehealth to rural, remote, and frontier students and families and to help schools and local providers coordinate care and bill Medicaid for school-based services. In doing so, we address long wait times, transportation barriers, and provider shortages that leave rural students and families without reliable access to behavioral health support.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Catholic Social Services Brother Francis Shelter Clare House
data.programDescription: Closing the Gap: Rural Health Care Transitions for Medically Fragile Alaskans — Catholic Social Services proposes to implement a Medicaid-aligned Medical Respite model to support future inclusion in Alaska’s Medicaid demonstration waiver, addressing the lack of a reimbursable recovery setting for medically fragile Alaskans experiencing homelessness who are too ill to recover safely in shelter or on the street.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Central Area Rural Transit System, Inc. (CARTS)
data.programDescription: Collaborative Rural Transit Development Plan for Sustainable Mobility in Seward and Homer — Central Area Rural Transit System (CARTS) proposes a community-led transportation planning process for Homer, Seward, and surrounding Kenai Peninsula communities, where no public transit currently exists and residents without personal vehicles face significant barriers to healthcare and essential services. A qualified transportation consultant will conduct needs assessments, community engagement, and service model evaluation to produce a comprehensive regional transportation plan with phased implementation options and funding strategies. The resulting plan will provide a roadmap for developing sustainable, locally appropriate transit solutions that improve healthcare access.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Healthcare Access Expansion Through Technology-Enabled Care — Central Peninsula Hospital proposes investments in digital health infrastructure, including clinical documentation improvement, telehealth expansion, and cybersecurity enhancements. Serving a geographically dispersed population across the Kenai Peninsula, CPH faces workforce shortages, increasing patient complexity, documentation burdens, and limited access to specialty care. This project will reduce administrative workload, improve care coordination and regulatory compliance, strengthen reimbursement and value-based care participation, and expand access to high-quality local health services.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expanding the Healthy Smiles Forever Model of On-site Oral Healthcare to Rural Long Term Care Facilities — Christian Health Associates proposes to plan the expansion of its existing Healthy Smiles Forever on-site dental care model—currently operating at 5 Anchorage and Mat-Su Valley facilities for 10 years—to 5 rural long-term care facilities in Homer, Cordova, Juneau, Ketchikan, and Soldotna. Planning activities include developing a replicable expansion template, analyzing organizational structure options, building recruitment strategies, and improving Medicaid reimbursement processes. Technology upgrades for existing sites are also planned to improve operational efficiency.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Rural Dental Care with Advanced 3D Imaging — Chugachmiut proposes to implement advanced 3D dental imaging services at the Chugachmiut Regional Health Center in Seward to address limited access to diagnostic imaging for rural residents of the Chugach Region. Patients currently travel outside the region for cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging needed for complex dental diagnosis and treatment planning. The project will expand local access to specialty dental diagnostics for rural, remote, and frontier Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expanding Rural Access to Comprehensive Behavioral Health Services — Chugachmiut proposes the development and implementation of a comprehensive program for the Chugach region and State of Alaska that provides psychological and neurological assessments, autism services, fetal alcohol spectrum disorder assessments, peri natal services, therapy services, and case management support, thereby expanding and localizing access to specialized behavioral health services for rural communities by providing telehealth and in-person clinical services, allowing families to receive timely evaluations, treatment planning, and follow-up care locally.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Rural Alaska Dental Access Through In-Clinic Digital Dentistry — Chugachmiut proposes to expand restorative dental services by implementing digital dental scanning and in-clinic 3D printing technology across four clinics in the Chugach Region, addressing treatment delays, laboratory dependence, and travel barriers that limit timely access to custom dental appliances for residents of rural and remote Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expanding Rural Access to Point-of-Care Laboratory Diagnostics — Chugachmiut proposes to implement point-of-care laboratory diagnostics in five rural clinics across the Chugach Region to address delays in diagnosis and treatment caused by geographic isolation, transportation barriers, and limited access to laboratory services. The project will provide local access to essential diagnostic testing, supporting timely clinical decision-making for residents of rural, remote, and frontier Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expanding Rural Access to Diagnostic Imaging Through Digital X-Ray Technology — Chugachmiut proposes expanding access to diagnostic imaging by implementing portable digital X-ray services at five rural clinics across the Chugach Region. The project addresses limited local access to diagnostic imaging in geographically isolated communities, where patients currently must travel long distances for basic imaging studies, resulting in delays in diagnosis and treatment.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rebuilds and modernizes Yakutat's EMS and systems through an integrated rural care model, providing updated technology, equipment, healthcare coordination, and workforce strategies to support local response capacity.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Yakutat EMS and Fire Response System Rebuild and Technology Modernization — The City and Borough of Yakutat Public Safety Department, in partnership with Yakutat Community Health Center, proposes to rebuild and modernize Yakutat's Emergency Medical Services and systems through an integrated rural care model. Yakutat is remote and isolated. Advanced medical critical care is hundreds of miles away, reached only by air or water. Yakutat EMS is the first and most critical care available to Yakutat's 640 residents. This project will provide updated technology and equipment, healthcare coordination, and workforce development strategies to support the response capacity.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Community Health Data and Billing Infrastructure — The City and Borough of Juneau's CCFR Community Health Division proposes to hire a contractor to build billing and data infrastructure within the Imagetrend platform for its three community health teams—Mobile Integrated Health, Mobile Crisis, and Sleep-off/Sobering Center—which currently conduct nearly 5,000 annual contacts with no reimbursement or billing structure. The contractor will develop Medicaid/Medicare billing systems and automated reporting dashboards to support program sustainability and quality improvement. This infrastructure investment is designed to provide a stable funding pathway for community health programs currently dependent entirely on CBJ appropriations.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Aleknagik Rural Health Access Strategic Plan — The City of Aleknagik proposes a 12-month strategic planning effort to address healthcare access barriers for this remote community of approximately 200 residents on the shores of Lake Aleknagik in Southwest Alaska. The plan addresses three areas: a sustainable rural workforce strategy including recruitment pathways and clinician housing options, an operational review and capital improvement plan for the municipally owned clinic, and transportation and connectivity improvements to strengthen access to higher levels of care. Deliverables include a costed, 5-year phased implementation roadmap adopted by City resolution.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: New EKG Monitors — The City of Bethel proposes to purchase three new state-of-the-art EKG monitors/defibrillators, now called cardiac monitors/defibrillators, to replace three ten-year old cardiac monitor/defibrillators stationed in three ambulances used by emergency medical service responders. The current equipment is at the end of its useful life, produces slower diagnostic results, is difficult to find parts for and repair, and has experienced heavy use due to Bethel's high call volume. Bethel EMS personnel serve Bethel residents and visitors 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Kenai Fire Department Rural Mobile Healthcare & EMS Transformation Initiative — City of Kenai Fire Department proposes to modernize rural emergency medical services through the acquisition and implementation of advanced prehospital critical care equipment, improving emergency cardiac, respiratory, trauma, and diagnositic capabilities for residents and visitors throughout the Kenai Peninsula Borough.  The project addresses gaps created by aging equipment, extended transport times, increasing call volumes, and limited access to advanced prehospital care in Southcentral Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Nenana Healthcare Alliance — City of Nenana proposes renovating existing indoor and outdoor community space to create a year-round location for community gathering, physical activity, hygiene access, showers and water filling services for residents without running water, behavioral health and recovery programming, prevention activities, and health-related services coordinated through local partnerships and a Technical Assistance provider, addressing critical gaps in community infrastructure, social connection, and access to health-supporting resources for Nenana and surrounding rural residents.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Togiak Family Resource Center Renovation: Jake's Place Satellite Facility and Community Wellness Center — The City of Togiak proposes to renovate the Family Resource Center to establish a Jake's Place satellite residential substance use disorder treatment program, in partnership with Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation, alongside a community wellness gathering space, addressing the absence of local treatment options for Togiak and the western Bristol Bay region, where residents must leave their home communities to access care. The year one planning phase reduces risk by establishing operational sustainability before capital investment occurs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Grow Your Own Behavioral Health Workforce and Training Supports — Community Connections proposes to develop and implement a locally rooted behavioral health workforce pipeline to address critical workforce shortages limiting access to children’s mental health services in Ketchikan and remote communities on Prince of Wales Island, building capacity through credential advancement, structured internships, onboarding improvements, and community-based career pathways.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: EHR Optimization and Scheduling/Service Coordination System Improvements — Community Connections proposes to optimize its electronic health record and implement a scheduling system to improve access to behavioral health services for youth and families in Ketchikan and the seven remote communities on Prince of Wales Island, addressing administrative burden, fragmented coordination, and technology gaps that limit timely care in rural, geographically isolated communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Speech, Swallow & Cognitive Access Initiative — Compass Therapy LLC proposes to expand access to specialized speech, swallowing, and cognitive-communication services through workforce development, caregiver training, telehealth infrastructure, and technology lending. The project addresses shortages of specialized rehabilitation providers and barriers to specialty care for older adults and individuals with neurological conditions across Alaska, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Chanlyut Residential Renovation & Integrated Behavioral Health Care Expansion — Cook Inlet Tribal Council, Inc. proposes a behavioral health expansion project to address gaps in care for Alaskans with substance use disorders/co-occurring mental health conditions. The project will accept referrals statewide. Specifically, CITC will enhance its billing capacity and Electronic Health Records system to support new pathways to healing, while addressing infrastructure upgrades that modify the service delivery environment in a therapeutic manner at Chanlyut, CITC’s residential treatment facility providing ASAM 3.1 level of care, and at CITC main social services building.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Pharmacy Transformation: Safe Compounding, Automated Dispensing, and Infusion Care — Cordova Community Medical Center proposes to modernize its pharmacy infrastructure and clinical workforce to launch safe, on-site chemotherapy and biologic infusion services by achieving USP <797>/<800> compliance through certified cleanroom installation and deploying an automated dispensing system to replace manual medication management. These investments will close the infrastructure gap that currently forces Cordova patients to travel by plane or ferry to Anchorage for treatments that are standard of care elsewhere.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Integrates behavioral health and primary care services by redesigning clinic space, workflows, and improving technology to deliver whole-person, team-based care for Cordova residents.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Cordova Community Medical Center Behavioral Health Integration — Cordova Community Medical Center proposes to integrate its Community Behavioral Health Clinic into its primary care clinic, addressing the fragmented, siloed behavioral health delivery system that creates access barriers for residents of Cordova a remote Alaska community accessible only by air or sea. The current system of co located clinics not only creates barriers but also duplication of efforts and exacerbates work force gaps.. The project will redesign clinic space, workflows, and improve shared technology to deliver accessible, efficient, whole-person, team-based care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Healthy Beginnings & Safe Communities: Cordova Youth and Family Wellness Initiative(SART/CAC) — Cordova Family Resource Center proposes expanding youth prevention programs and enhancing coordinated support for survivors of violence, addressing gaps in access to behavioral health, advocacy, medical, and forensic services for children, youth, families, and rural residents in the remote community of Cordova. The project will strengthen community-based prevention efforts, increase access to trauma-informed support, and improve coordination among local partners to ensure individuals and families can receive timely services and support close to home.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expands youth prevention and enhances support for survivors of violence, addressing gaps in behavioral health, advocacy, medical, and forensic services for children, youth, and rural residents in Cordova.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Growing Health in the Yukon Flats: SDPI Expansion for Food Security, Community Wellness, and Diabetes Prevention — The Council of Athabascan Tribal Governments proposes to expand its Special Diabetes Program for Indians by increasing access to healthy foods, nutrition education, traditional foods activities, physical activity opportunities, and diabetes prevention services to address food insecurity, chronic disease risk, and barriers to healthy living among Alaska Native residents of Arctic Village, Beaver, Fort Yukon, and Venetie through community gardening, wellness activities, healthy cooking education, food preservation training, and community-based health promotion.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Denali Borough Rural Health Care Transformation Project Coordinator — Denali Borough proposes establishing a Rural Health Project Coordinator position to strengthen regional health care partnerships, coordinate public health initiatives, advance rural health infrastructure projects, and support health workforce development, addressing persistent gaps in health care access, service coordination, and system capacity across the Denali Borough.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Nenana Community Health & Wellness Strategic Planning Initiative — Denali Insight Consulting proposes a community health and wellness needs assessment and strategic planning initiative for Nenana, a rural Interior Alaska community of approximately 350 residents that serves as a regional service hub but lacks a formal health committee or shared strategic framework. The project will conduct community surveys, stakeholder interviews, and facilitated engagement to identify service gaps and priorities, followed by formation of a cross-sector Community Health & Wellness Steering Committee with defined roles and measurable outcomes. Deliverables include a final assessment report and a strategic direction document to guide coordinated health investments in Nenana and surrounding communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strengthening Alaska’s Correctional Health System Through Virtual Care — The Department of Corrections (DOC) proposes to implement telemedicine and teledental equipment across correctional facilities. This expansion connects incarcerated Alaskans with healthcare providers in their home communities and across the state, improving continuity of care both during incarceration and after release. Many individuals enter custody with untreated chronic medical and mental health conditions; by introducing them to telehealth services and establishing relationships with community-based providers, DOC supports smoother transitions to care upon reentry.

data.programDescription: Engaging in the Health Information System to Improve Care Coordination for Rural Alaskans — The Department of Corrections (DOC) proposes to integrate its electronic medical records with Alaska’s Health Information Exchange and Prescription Drug Monitoring Program to strengthen care transitions as individuals move between DOC and rural community providers. This will address gaps in care coordination, incomplete medical histories, and limited visibility into controlled substance use for incarcerated Alaskans across remote communities. These gaps disproportionately impact rural Alaskans, who rely heavily on continuity of care across Tribal, regional, and local health systems.

data.programDescription: Alaska School District Healthcare Programs of Study — The Alaska Department of Education & Early Development (DEED) will provide competitive subgrants to school districts, partnering vocation training institutions and local regional employers to deliver programs of study in healthcare careers to secondary students. Public school districts currently receive federal Carl Perkins funding to provide exposure and training to students to connect them to workforce opportunities after graduation.  Of Alaska’s 53 districts, 36 small and rural districts receive only $20,000 of these federal funds to provide Career and Technical Education across fourteen different career clusters of which Healthcare and Human Services is just one.  Currently, 26 of Alaska’s smallest districts do not offer any federally funded healthcare career and technical education due to limited capacity or resources. Each school district is part of DEED’s existing network that supports and promotes career and technical education programming.  The healthcare program of study grants would allow smaller rural districts to focus on providing options to rural students to explore healthcare career options and receive technical training leading to careers in the local, regional, and statewide healthcare sector.  The grants would serve students with priority given to smaller rural districts facing economy of scale limitations.
