data.programDescription: AI-Assisted EEG: Bridging the Neurological Assessment Gap with AI — Mat-Su Regional Medical Center (MSRMC) proposes acquiring and implementing an AI-supported platform with a single-use, eight-lead headband, which a nurse can rapidly apply. This system will then enable physicians to quickly determine if a patient is experiencing status epilepticus. This rapid identification is crucial for making emergent treatment decisions, prompting appropriate local care and potentially avoiding the need for a costly, time-sensitive transfer away from the Mat-Su into Anchorage.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mat-Su Community Health Response System — Matanuska-Susitna Borough will build a mobile integrated healthcare program that reaches the low-resource residents found along its entire settlement gradient — from the urbanized Palmer-Wasilla core through suburban and rural belts to the off-road, off-grid frontier. Community-paramedic teams deliver treat-in-place care, point-of-care diagnostics, and telehealth, with high-utilizer case management and a behavioral-health and substance-use crisis co-response concentrated where need is densest. Year 1 builds the coordinator, protocols, diagnostics, credentialing, and partnerships.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mat-Su Borough EMS Mobile Health Infrastructure Modernization Initiative — Matanuska-Susitna Borough proposes to modernize its mobile EMS infrastructure by procuring two telehealth-ready quick-response vehicles and completing a build-ready ambulance design to support future fleet modernization. The project addresses limited non-transport response capacity, unreliable field connectivity, and an aging ambulance configuration across the Borough’s urban, rural, and frontier communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: MSB EMS CORE Program — Clinical Operations and Rural Exchange — Matanuska-Susitna Borough proposes a two-way clinical exchange that places rural Alaska paramedics into a high-volume urban emergency medical system and hosts urban paramedics in Alaska. The exchange builds and maintains advanced clinical skills that low patient volume and geographic isolation make difficult to sustain, strengthening the emergency medical workforce that serves Borough residents and surrounding rural communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Building the Mat-Su Healthcare Workforce: High School Pathways for Rural Alaska — Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District proposes building a regional healthcare workforce training network and certification hub, addressing healthcare workforce shortages, limited training capacity, and barriers to career entry for students and healthcare employers across the Mat-Su Borough and rural Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Frontier Clinic Completion: Primary Care Access for McCarthy-Kennecott, Alaska — McCarthy Emergency Services proposes to complete and equip a frontier primary care clinic in McCarthy, Alaska, addressing the total absence of primary care infrastructure in one of the state's most remote and fastest-growing communities. The clinic will serve permanent residents, seasonal workers, and visitors across a vast, road-limited region of East-Central Alaska with no local access to a physician, nurse practitioner, or Community Health Aide.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Pay for Value - Alternative Payment Models — Medical Park Family Care, an Anchorage-based family medicine clinic serving patients from over 60 Alaska communities, proposes to evaluate and implement an alternative payment model focused on rewarding primary care and preventive services—addressing a reimbursement environment where their largest payer has not increased rates in 10 years. The planning phase will analyze patient data to identify potential employer and insurer partners, followed by program design discussions; implementation is anticipated in the second year. The project aims to create a shared-savings APM model that reduces administrative burden, improves provider retention, and improves patient health outcomes.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Advancing Value-based Payment Readiness through PCMH Implementation on the Kenai Peninsula — Moda proposes to partner with Central Peninsula Hospital and South Peninsula Hospital to support implementation of the National Committee for Quality Assurance’s (NCQA) Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) model across four clinic sites. This project will help strengthen partners’ quality improvement and reporting infrastructure, support expanded access to care for rural populations and increase partners' readiness to participate in advanced value-based payment arrangements in preparation for Alaska’s planned 1115 Medicaid coordinated care demonstration project on the Kenai Peninsula.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mountain View Community Health Transformation and Sustainability Initiative - Building a Neighborhood Health System Without Walls — Mountain View Health Services proposes a Physician-led, Nurse-enabled, Social Work-integrated, Early Life Community Health Worker (EL-CHW)-supported neighborhood health system "without walls". The project combines integrated primary care, behavioral health, substance use treatment, telehealth, home visiting, and mobile health with a new Medicaid-supported EL-CHW model providing prevention and care coordination from preconception through age five to improve access and outcomes for underserved residents of Anchorage.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Securing Fiscally Sustainable Healthcare For Future Generations of Upper Ahtna Indigenous People — Mt. Sanford Tribal Health Consortium, serving a frontier community of approximately 60 residents four hours northeast of Anchorage, proposes a comprehensive fiscal sustainability and care delivery redesign to address structural insolvency under a fee-for-service model that generates approximately $82,000 annually against operating costs that require outside support. The project will evaluate alternative care delivery models (direct provider, coordinated access hub, or hybrid), complete an Alternative Payment Model readiness assessment, implement financial and population health analytics infrastructure, and develop workforce alignment strategies for CHA and BHA roles. The goal is to identify a viable, sustainable path forward for one of Alaska's most geographically isolated and financially fragile frontier health programs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Municipality of Anchorage: Connecting Crisis Care and Safety Net System to Rural Healthcare — Municipality of Anchorage (MOA) proposes to implement technology and test pilot approaches to improve outcomes from behavioral health crisis response, especially for rural and Tribal enrollees seeking care in Anchorage. The MOA will implement interoperable client records to coordinate care with local, Tribal, and other healthcare providers, sustain services, and capture data. MOA will implement and evaluate pilot projects to fill critical gaps in Anchorage's Crisis Care and Safety Net System to improve patient outcomes and system efficiency, and identify possible new Medicaid waiver services.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Jeffs Path Expansion — My House is expanding residential behavioral health services for young adults ages 18–25 in the Mat-Su Valley by increasing capacity from 8 to 16 beds and adding ASAM Level 3.5 alongside Level 3.1 care. This service reduces the risks associated with placing young adults in mixed-age adult settings, where exposure to older, higher-acuity populations can negatively impact safety, engagement, and recovery. This expansion strengthens coordinated care with hospitals, behavioral health providers, and justice system partners to improve continuity of care and recovery outcomes.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Clinic planning and design for future health care in Chenega — The Native Village of Chenega proposes a community-driven planning process to assess evolving healthcare needs and develop a concept-level architectural design for a future clinic rebuild or renovation in this remote Prince William Sound community accessible only by boat or plane. The project will engage residents and healthcare providers through surveys and outreach to ensure any future facility investment reflects current and anticipated healthcare delivery changes since the existing clinic was built in 2006. Deliverables include a community needs assessment report and concept clinic design developed in collaboration with Chugachmiut, ANTHC, and planning professionals.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Native Village of Eyak Ilanka Community Health Center
data.programDescription: Ilanka Community Health Center and Cordova Community Medical Center Exploratory/Planning Phases for One Healthcare System — The Native Village of Eyak (NVE) proposes an exploratory/planning phases to begin the process of investigating a one healthcare system for the community of Cordova. Ilanka Community Health Center owned and operated by NVE and Cordova Community Medical Center (CCMC) are seeking the resources and support needed to begin the initial exploratory steps of a potential merger, including evaluating how combining services could strengthen financial stability, improve operational efficiency, and ultimately enhance care for the Cordova community all while keeping healthcare services close to home.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Tanana Supportive Housing Program for Individuals Entering Recovery — The Native Village of Tanana, in partnership with the Tanana Chiefs Conference, proposes to establish a culturally grounded supportive housing program paired with outpatient clinical treatment and cultural connection, Elder guidance, and meaningful community roles for adults entering recovery from substance use, addressing the lack of transitional, step-down care between residential treatment and return to home community for rural Alaska Native people in the Interior region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Nenana Mobile Crisis Team — The Nenana Volunteer Fire/EMS Department proposes a 6-month planning phase to design and operationalize a Mobile Crisis Team (MCT), given that behavioral health calls currently account for approximately 33% of all emergency responses in this community without a structured crisis response model or specialized training. Planning activities will develop operational policies, cross-agency coordination agreements with behavioral health providers and schools, workforce and training strategies, potential Medicaid billing pathways, and a phased implementation roadmap. The goal is a coordinated, treat-in-place crisis response model that reduces unnecessary emergency department use and out-of-community placements.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: ADA-Accessible Mobile Integrated Health Expansion for Frontier Communities — Ninilchik Traditional Council proposes to expand mobile health services by adding a larger, accessible mobile medical unit and establishing regular clinics concentrating in Kasilof, and other underserved communities on the southern Kenai Peninsula. The project addresses the lack of local health services and limited access to care caused by long travel distances and the existing mobile unit cannot accommodate people with disabilities or complex health needs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Anchor Point Rural Urgent Care and Integrated Access Stabilization — Ninilchik Traditional Council proposes to establish a coordinated access system integrating urgent care, primary care, and behavioral health services, addressing fragmented care and limited local access across the southern Kenai Peninsula for Alaska Native and American Indian residents and other underserved rural populations facing barriers due to distance, workforce shortages, and disconnected services.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Foundations for Regional EMS Training — The North Slope Borough Fire Department proposes to establish a regional pediatric and neonatal emergency care training program for emergency responders and Community Health Aides that develops local instructor capacity, delivers simulation-based education, and expands specialty training opportunities. This project addresses gaps in pediatric and neonatal emergency care training across the North Slope Borough, where geographic isolation, limited access to specialty education, and workforce challenges affect long-term clinical competency and program sustainability.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: New Computers/Servers for Norton Sound Health Corporation — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes installing modern core data storage, high-speed routing networks, and clinical workstations to replace end-of-life IT infrastructure that threatens system reliability and patient data security across fifteen remote village clinics and the regional hub of Nome.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Doppler Ultrasound Upgrade — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes to deploy sixty-five dual-probe handheld Dopplers with ruggedized cases to community health aides and advanced practice providers across remote clinics, addressing a critical regional gap in standardized diagnostic infrastructure needed to monitor maternal-fetal health and evaluate vulnerable elders and diabetic patients for vascular perfusion and peripheral deep vein blood clot risks.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Direct Patient Monitoring for High-Risk Patients — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes to implement a cellular-enabled remote patient monitoring system and daily health check-in surveys to address real-time clinical visibility gaps and coordinate care for five hundred high-risk patients managing complex chronic diseases and serious mental illnesses across Nome and fifteen remote village clinics within the Bering Strait region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Behavioral Health Integration and Care — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes integrating behavioral health services into primary care settings by hiring specialized clinicians and implementing universal screening protocols. This addresses the fragmented delivery system and long wait times for mental health services, ensuring residents of the Norton Sound region receive immediate, coordinated access to both behavioral and physical health care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: 2C Centralized Patient Navigation Project — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes to establish a centralized scheduling hub utilizing four cross-trained schedulers to integrate appointment systems across all fifteen remote village clinics, the Nome Family Medicine clinic, and the Norton Sound Regional Hospital. Equipped with population health dashboards, this model enables cross-facility booking and proactive clinical care gap closures during a single phone call, mitigating regional staffing shortages and reducing patient travel expenses.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Maternal and Neonatal Equipment Upgrades — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes to procure standardized maternal-fetal telemetry monitors, neonatal resuscitation warmers, infant phototherapy units, specialized delivery carts, and critical care transport cots to replace obsolete clinical infrastructure across three hospital mother-baby suites and regional air and ground medical transport teams for the twenty tribes of the flight-dependent Bering Strait region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Population Health Based Care Model — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes "Checkpoint for Health," a community health representative-led care navigation model designed to remove social, economic, and geographic barriers to clinical care for all residents across the 16 tribal communities of the Bering Strait region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Heart Disease Screening Technology — Norton Sound Health Corporation proposes establishing a regional cardiac diagnostic center by deploying adhesive extended-wear cardiac monitors and expanding itinerant cardiology and echocardiography services to address diagnostic delays and limited access to specialty care across the 16 communities of the Bering Strait region.

data.awardeeName: Office of Children's Services, Department of Family & Community Services
data.programDescription: Alaska Child Welfare Referral Process Improvement Project — The Office of Children's Services (OCS) proposes  investing in a bridge solution that works with Alaska's existing systems and the health information exchange to close gaps now, while remaining compatible with the future Comprehensive Child Welfare Information System (CCWIS).

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Office of Children's Services, Department of Family & Community Services
data.programDescription: Alaska Comprehensive Child Welfare Information System (CCWIS) Project — The Office of Children's Services proposes to modernize the Comprehensive Child Welfare Information System (CCWIS) . CCWIS modernization is especially consequential for Alaska’s rural and remote communities, where families are served across vast distances, limited connectivity, and a dispersed network of providers, regional hubs, and tribal partners.  This investment is designed to provide lasting value beyond the initial RHTP performance period by advancing a modular CCWIS that integrates with existing State of Alaska systems and is built to federal design and interoperability standards.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Office of Health Savings, Department of Health
data.programDescription: Provider Gap Analysis — The Office of Health Savings proposes to conduct a comprehensive, statewide Provider Gap Analysis to identify geographic, service-level, and population-based access gaps across Alaska’s health system. Activities will include provider mapping, provider-to-population and service mix analysis using Medicaid claims data, and targeted stakeholder engagement to validate findings and identify unmet needs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: MyEyesAI Hub-and-Spoke Tele-Ophthalmology for Rural Alaska. — Ophthalmic Associates proposes to establish a hub-and-spoke teleophthalmology network using MyEyesAI to support standardized eye intake, image capture, specialist review, triage, and referral coordination, thereby addressing delayed access to ophthalmology and avoidable travel for rural, remote, and frontier Alaskans across participating clinics, optometry practices, and community health sites.

Construction of New Exam Room — Optical Aleutians proposes the creation of a dedicated optical exam room to replace the
borrowed dentist office currently in use, as it poses multiple issues regarding ADA
compliance, sanitation, consistency of access, and ability to service needs of residents
with chronic issues. This will be built in Unalaska, which serves as a healthcare hub for
the rest of the western Aleutians.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Cultural Healing House: A Culturally-Centered Addiction Recovery Program for Southeast Alaska — The Organized Village of Kake proposes establishing a Cultural Healing House that expands access to culturally grounded recovery and behavioral health services, addresses gaps in care for Alaska Native people and rural communities, strengthens community belonging, and increases local service capacity through peer support training across Southeast Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Value-Based Payment and Community Outreach (AVPCO) — OrthoAlaska proposes to develop bundled payment and value-based contracts with commercial insurers and self-insured Alaska employers and to deploy community health workers for rural chronic disease screening and outreach. The project addresses the financial instability of rural primary care and inconsistent access to preventive care across Anchorage, Mat-Su, the Kenai Peninsula, and Kodiak Island.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Improving Maternal, Fetal and Neonatal Safety with Advanced Monitoring and Teladoc — PeaceHealth Ketchikan Medical Center proposes expanding a technology enabled maternal, fetal and neonatal care system that integrates advanced fetal monitoring, centralized surveillance, and real-time neonatology consultation, strengthening diagnostic capabilities, intrapartum monitoring, and specialty access across Southern Southeast Alaska’s rural communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Surgical Transformation: Expanding Access and Modernizing Care — PeaceHealth Ketchikan Medical Center proposes introducing the first robotic assisted minimally invasive surgeries in orthopedic, gastroenterology, urology, gynecology, and general surgery to Southern Southeast Alaska. This evidence-supported solution will expand local specialty capacity, reduce out-of-area referrals, and improve outcomes by overcoming longstanding access barriers.  By enabling high-quality procedures close to home, the project transforms healthcare in the region and works to reduce health disparities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Launching an Alaska CHW Provider Network and Managed Services Hub — Pear Suite proposes building a statewide Community Health Worker provider infrastructure and shared services network that enables community-based organizations and local CHW hubs through technology, clinical and compliance support, contracting, revenue cycle management, and operational services, addressing infrastructure gaps that limit CHW integration with healthcare systems across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Scaling Alaska’s Community Health Worker Workforce Through Training and Credentialing Infrastructure — Pear Suite Inc. proposes establishing a statewide Community Health Worker (CHW) workforce development system that combines Alaskan CHW-led training, shared workforce infrastructure, and a credentialing support helpdesk. The project addresses a common challenge: CHWs complete training but often lack ongoing support to navigate credentialing, compliance, and employment pathways. By connecting training to long-term support, the initiative creates a sustainable pathway into Alaska’s healthcare workforce, including rural and frontier communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Petersburg Medical Center Telehealth Integration — Petersburg Medical Center proposes to establish an integrated Telehealth Program, serving all departments of Petersburg Borough’s only hospital and primary care clinic, bridging critical gaps in access to specialty care for chronic disease screening and management for the remote communities in and around this Southeast Alaska Borough through in-depth partnership with telemedicine providers.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Petersburg Medical Center Behavioral Health Department Launch — Petersburg Medical Center proposes the launch of a full Behavioral Health Department, integrated within Petersburg Borough’s only hospital and primary care clinic to bridge critical gaps in access to in-person psychiatric and clinical behavioral health services for the remote communities in and around this Southeast Alaska Borough.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Petersburg Medical Center Maternal Health & Early Childhood Planning Project — Petersburg Medical Center, an independent non-profit Critical Access Hospital serving remote Southeast Alaska communities accessible only by boat or plane, proposes to launch lactation consultant services—filling a complete gap in the service area—and engage Community Wellness leadership in planning for future expansion of maternal and early childhood community-based supports. The project will integrate lactation services into the primary care clinic and Cerner EMR, train additional staff to lactation consultant certification, and assess the viability of further service expansion such as home visiting. This work addresses documented postpartum care gaps for a population that must leave the community to give birth.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Prince of Wales Health Network Mobile Integrated  Health (MIH) Program — Prince of Wales Health Network will begin planning the framework for a Mobile Integrated Health (MIH) program to improve access, continuity, and quality of healthcare services for residents of Prince of Wales Island.  The MIH program will deliver proactive, community-based care by structuring a program that will meet the unique needs of our remote island communities and demographic groups and utilize our limited resources in a way that will benefit our residents.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Advanced Prenatal Access - Implementing a Hybrid Obstetric Access Model in Seward and Anchorage — Providence Health & Services – Washington proposes to establish a maternal telehealth and pregnancy monitoring program for Seward and surrounding communities. In conjunction with Providence Seward Medical Center and Providence Alaska Medical Center, the project will expand access to pregnancy care through telehealth consultations, fetal monitoring, ultrasound services, and care coordination for pregnant individuals who currently face significant travel, weather, and geographic barriers to obtaining obstetric and specialty care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Coordinating to Drive Redesign and Sustainability of Alaska's Graduate Medical Education Programs — Providence Health & Services -Washington proposes to strengthen workforce capacity by stabilizing and enhancing the Alaska Family Medicine Residency Program. This project invests in recruitment, rural training, faculty development, and clinical training infrastructure to address Alaska’s shortage of primary care physicians and limited in-state residency capacity. This work supports a critical physician pipeline serving rural, frontier, and geographically dispersed communities across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Seward Social Services Hub: Advancing Health Through Coordinated Social Support Services — Providence Seward Medical Center proposes to establish a coordinated social services hub in Seward, Alaska to address housing instability, food insecurity, unsafe living conditions, and limited access to behavioral health support services. The project will centralize emergency and transitional housing support, domestic violence response services, food access programs, care coordination, and community-based services for vulnerable residents in Seward and surrounding rural communities impacted by adverse social determinants of health.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Dual-Eligible Value-Based Care (VBC) Model Design and Readiness Initiative — Providence Health & Services – Washington proposes to design a provider-led, statewide value-based care framework for Alaska’s dual-eligible population. The project addresses fragmented Medicare-Medicaid financing, rising costs, avoidable utilization, and care coordination barriers affecting rural Alaskans with complex needs. The analytic, payment-design, and implementation roadmap will be built to support future voluntary alternative payment models and integrated care arrangements.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Implementing Remote Patient Monitoring Reimbursement to Drive Sustainability of Services and Positive Outcomes — Providence Health & Services –Washington proposes establishing Remote Patient Monitoring for three disease states: Congestive Heart Failure, Hypertension, and Type II Diabetes Mellitus. The population of focus would include empaneled Alaskan patients with Medicaid as the primary payer with a diagnosis of one of the three disease states mentioned above.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Improve Continuity of Care in Rural Alaska via Community Connect — Providence Health & Services – Washington proposes to expand a shared electronic health record system through Community Connect by covering initial vendor licensing costs that prevent small providers from adopting integrated systems. This project addresses fragmented patient records, duplicate testing, poor coordination, and limited system availability. It will support rural hospitals and clinics across Alaska, where scarce resources and high upfront licensing fees prevent use of shared systems that enable continuous, coordinated patient care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Pediatric Specialty Access Planning Initiative -  Expanded Telemedicine Capabilities (PSAPI) — Ptarmigan Pediatrics proposes a one-year, $20,000 planning initiative to evaluate the feasibility of a multidisciplinary telemedicine framework for complex pediatric evaluations—including FASD, neuropsychology, and speech therapy—delivered from a Wasilla hub to rural Alaska communities through 'sister site' partnerships with remote clinics. A Nurse Practitioner coordinator will conduct 3–4 rural site visits to assess broadband connectivity, clinical space, and staffing capacity, and develop MOUs and workflow designs for hybrid telemedicine delivery. The planning year is designed to produce a site-readiness roadmap and evidence-based procurement plan for Year 2 equipment and implementation funding.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Building Capacity for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) Status — Railbelt Mental Health & Addictions proposes a planning and readiness phase toward achieving Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) designation in a frontier region spanning 180 road miles of the Parks Highway, serving communities of 100–800 residents approximately 50–150 miles from Fairbanks and Wasilla. Planning activities include conducting a needs assessment, determining CCBHC certification requirements, engaging stakeholders, and building the administrative and operational infrastructure necessary for a full CCBHC application. CCBHC designation would enable same-day assessments, 24/7 crisis services, and comprehensive behavioral health care regardless of ability to pay.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Technology Upgrades — Railbelt Mental Health and Addictions proposes modernizing and expanding telehealth, technology, and data infrastructure to address outdated systems that limit service delivery, workforce efficiency, and access to care for rural residents across Nenana and the Denali Borough service area, spanning approximately 150 road miles along the Parks Highway.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Resource Center for Parents and Children
data.programDescription: Pathways to Healing for Children, Parents, and Families — The Resource Center for Parents and Children proposes expanding behavioral health services for children, families, pregnant and postpartum parents, and caregivers through evidence-based trauma treatment, case management, and family support services. The project addresses significant gaps in access to behavioral health care, particularly for individuals impacted by child abuse, neglect, family violence, substance misuse, adverse childhood experiences, child-on-child problematic sexual behaviors, and child welfare involvement across rural and remote Interior Alaska and North Slope communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Using Advanced Air Mobility Systems to Deliver Perishable Pharmaceuticals to Remote Destinations — Ryan Air proposes to deploy autonomous cargo drones and electric vertical take-off and landing (EVTOL) aircraft to deliver pharmaceuticals and transport patients and healthcare providers across roadless communities in the Bethel and Dillingham regions. This project addresses the near-total lack of reliable, affordable pharmaceutical access and medical transport in remote Alaska Native villages, where geography, weather, and the absence of road infrastructure create life-threatening gaps in basic healthcare.

data.programDescription: Pediatric Workforce Development in Alaska — By investing in faculty development, resident and fellow physician training capacity, and statewide educational partnerships, the Pediatric Residency Alaska Track creates lasting improvements in Alaska’s pediatric workforce with a direct impact on access to care for communities throughout the state.

data.programDescription: Increase telehealth services for Individuals with Intellectual and/or Developmental Disabilities on HCBS waivers — The Division of Senior and Disabilities Services (SDS) proposes to provide access to telehealth services to more individuals receiving Home and Community Based Services (HCBS). This project will expand telehealth services through a contract with RingMD to address the unique health and behavioral needs of HCBS recipients across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Health EHR & Systems Modernization TA Initiative — Set Free Alaska proposes to modernize the operational workflows and health information technology that support behavioral health service delivery, addressing fragmented systems, limited interoperability, and operational inefficiencies affecting rural, remote, and frontier Alaskans. The project will establish an implementation-ready roadmap for integrated, technology-enabled systems that strengthen care coordination and support sustainable healthcare delivery.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Healthy Beginnings Through Integrated Infant and Toddler Expansion in Partnership with Chugachmiut Early Head Start — Seward Prevention Coalition proposes partnering with Chugachmiut Early Head Start to establish an Early Head Start classroom, expanding early learning and care for infants and toddlers and addressing the limited birth to three child care capacity, developmental screening access, and family support services available to families in Seward and surrounding rural communities on the Kenai Peninsula.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: Sitka Counseling and Prevention Services Inc.
data.programDescription: Sitka Counseling Therapeutic Services Expansion and Renovation Project — Sitka Counseling proposes to expand behavioral health service capacity by planning improvements to facilities, workforce development, and technology systems. The project addresses limited space, workforce shortages, and barriers to accessing outpatient, residential, and family services. Planning will focus on children and families in Sitka while developing partnerships for clinical training, consultation, and supervision to support service delivery in rural and underserved communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expansion and Improvement of Rehabilitation Services to Support Continuum of Care Close to Home — South Peninsula Hospital proposes to renovate and equip existing hospital space to open the first cardiopulmonary rehabilitation program on the southern Kenai Peninsula. Residents recovering from heart attacks/surgery and chronic lung disease currently must travel 150 miles round trip twice weekly for rehabilitation services, a prohibitive barrier for many. As the region’s population ages, the need for this service has increased. This project brings medically supervised exercise, education, and recovery support close to home for about 17,000 rural Alaskans.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Modernize and Automate Medication Dispensing for Safety and Efficiency — South Peninsula Hospital proposes to launch a project to implement an automated medication dispensing system fully integrated with its Epic EHR in the SPH Pharmacy, which serves the 17,000 rural residents of the southern Kenai Peninsula. Currently, SPH relies heavily on manual processes and dated systems, which limit the scalability as SPH seeks to expand specialty services (such as infusion) to meet growing needs. AMDS will improve medication safety, streamline pharmacy workflows, reduce drug errors and waste, and position SPH to increase healthcare access and quality in our rural region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expansion of Specialty Pediatric Services — Southcentral Foundation proposes to expand its Specialty Pediatric Clinic, a critical statewide access point that addresses gaps in specialized care for Alaska Native and American Indian children with complex medical and developmental needs across Alaska, including those from rural, remote, and frontier communities who must travel for care.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription:
Chitina Community Health Clinic Expansion — Southcentral Foundation proposes to expand resources at the Chitina Community Clinic (located along the Edgerton Highway, south of Glennallen but east of Tonsina and northwest of Wrangell-St. Elias National Park and Preserve), improving the use of space for customer-owners* and providers, purchasing a vehicle, and providing community outreach for permanent residents and visitors to increase encounters at the clinic and thereby improve the financial stability of the community health center.

*SCF term for individuals they serve, instead of patient

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Yeshjesh T'uh Crisis Project — Southcentral Foundation’s Yeshjesh T’uh Crisis Project proposes strengthening system capacity by providing new innovative services, connecting the gaps in fragmented systems, and increasing access to culturally competent mental health and substance use disorder services in Mental Health Professional Shortage Areas here in Alaska. The proposed Yeshjesh T’uh Crisis Project provides high-intensity behavioral health services, including crisis stabilization and crisis residential care, for individuals from rural and remote Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rural Pharmacy Upgrade — Southcentral Foundation (SCF) proposes to improve pharmacy facilities and replace outdated secure, pharmacy-monitored, medicine-dispensing units (called “PickPoints”) in 14 rural clinics from Chitina to St. Paul, bringing SCF’s telepharmacies into functional alignment with security, software, and environmental needs, and making any minor modification necessary to ensure security, safety, and connectivity.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Traditional Healing Project — Southcentral Foundation proposes to integrate traditional healing practices at its rural community health centers, standard clinical services, and the Alaska Native Medical Center (ANMC), by expanding the Traditional Healing practitioner base; creating an Alaska traditional healing network and exchange; and improving long-term sustainability. This project will have state-wide impact through ANMC services and addresses the need for traditional wellness practices, such as ceremony, ritual, emotional and spiritual support beyond its clinic at the Anchorage Native Primary Care Center.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mammo On the Go Southeast — SEARHC proposes to establish a SEARHC-owned mobile mammography coach to bring breast cancer screening to women in Angoon, Kake, Hoonah, Gustavus, and Skagway expanding regionally after the year 1 project period. The project addresses the current lack of dedicated mobile mammography service and the travel barriers that make routine screening difficult for women in isolated Southeast Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Child Care Apprenticeship Program Expansion — Southeast Childhood Collective proposes expanding its Child Care Apprenticeship Program to train more early childhood educators in Southeast Alaska communities where child care shortages affect health care and other essential workers. The project addresses the shortage of trained child care staff, which limits the availability of reliable care for working families.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Develop Near Site Child Care for Bartlett Regional Hospital — Southeast Childhood Collective (SCC) proposes developing dedicated child care capacity for Bartlett Regional Hospital (BRH) employees by supporting a licensed child care provider to add spaces prioritized for hospital staff. The project addresses limited access to reliable child care, a barrier to recruiting and retaining health care workers at BRH, which serves Juneau and communities across Southeast Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Parents as Teachers 4th Trimester Initiative — Southeast Childhood Collective proposes expanding Parents as Teachers home visiting for families from birth through 16 weeks postpartum (the 4th trimester) to address delayed access to early family support, geographic isolation, and limited postpartum mental health resources in Juneau, Petersburg, Ketchikan, Gustavus, Pelican, and Tenakee Springs.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Southeast Alaska EMS Academy Network — The Southeast Region EMS Council proposes to launch the Southeast Alaska EMS Academy Network, a regional workforce initiative connecting three training hubs with rural communities. The project will expand access to EMS education, instructor development, simulation, leadership support, travel assistance, and collaboration while building shared, increasingly sustainable infrastructure for emergency care across Southeast Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Inclusive Healthcare for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities - Phase 1 — Special Olympics Alaska proposes to expand health screenings, train community health workers, and provide in-state neurological screening events to address limited preventive and specialty care for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities in rural and remote Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Community Partners Improving Home Accessibility — Statewide Independent Living Council of Alaska proposes to install durable, ADA-compliant modular aluminum and composite ramps at the homes of Alaskans with disabilities and aging Alaskans statewide, replacing wood ramps that fail within three to five years in Alaska's climate, for rural, remote, and frontier communities where existing home modification programs leave residents waiting years for safe entry access.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: AI Assistive Technology Needs Assessment Tool — The Statewide Independent Living Council of Alaska proposes to develop an artificial-intelligence assistive technology needs assessment tool that matches people to devices based on their functional needs, preferences, and home environment, connects users to additional resources including possible funding pathways, and addresses a shortage of qualified assessors that leaves rural Alaskans with disabilities, chronic conditions, and aging-related needs unable to obtain technology suited to their lives across rural, remote, and frontier communities statewide.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Mat-Su Rural Teaching Health Center: Denali Family Medicine Residency Program Development — Sunshine Community Health Center proposes to develop a community-based Family Medicine Residency Program, addressing Alaska’s critical shortage of rural primary care physicians by building a permanent, self-sustaining physician workforce pipeline in the Mat-Su Borough.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Frontier Healthcare Access and Modernization Initiative — Sunshine Community Health Center proposes expanding diagnostic, specialty, dental, and in-home care capacity to address gaps in local treatment capability that currently force patients to travel long distances or be transferred to Wasilla or Anchorage for conditions that could be managed closer to home, across its Talkeetna, Willow, and surrounding frontier service area, including patients in roadless communities who cannot be reached for clinical intervention.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: RN Care Management Billing Innovation & Outcome Analytics Infrastructure — Sunshine Community Health Center proposes to build documentation and data analytics infrastructure to capture registered nurse care management services currently delivered but not tracked or reimbursed under Alaska Medicaid. This infrastructure will measure patient health outcomes attributable to those services, supporting a formal request to expand the clinic's reimbursable scope of services and demonstrating the value of nursing care for patients with chronic conditions in the northern Mat-Su Valley.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Healthy Beginnings: Comprehensive Prenatal & Postpartum Care for Alaska Native Families — Tanana Chiefs Conference proposes implementing the Healthy Beginnings program to provide prenatal education, doula labor support, lactation services, parenting education, home visits, and coordinated maternal-infant care that address gaps in pregnancy, birth, and postpartum support for Alaska Native families, including those from remote villages, across 32 rural Interior Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Indigenous Healing Integration & Rural Wellness Transformation Initiative — Tanana Chiefs Conference proposes a permanent Department of Indigenous Health and Traditional Medicines that integrates Indigenous healing into primary care, behavioral health, chronic disease prevention, and telehealth. The project builds a clinical apprenticeship pathway for Alaska Native providers to learn applications of hands-on healing, including plants, diet, and lifestyle approaches to wellbeing and addresses the shortage of culturally safe and comprehensive Indigenous healing services for Alaska Native people in Fairbanks and 27 rural Interior Alaska communities served by TCC.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Village and Home Based Culturally Grounded End of Life Care — Tanana Chiefs Conference (TCC) proposes to strengthen access, quality and sustainability of palliative and end-of-life care to address the lack of local support identified in a 2024 TCC Annual Convention Resolution. This will enable seriously ill Elders in the Yukon Koyukuk, Yukon Tanana, Yukon Flats, and Upper Tanana subregions to remain in their home villages with trained caregivers, coordinated care teams, and palliative care services aligned with their goals.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Strong Traditions, Healthy Communities: Lifestyle & Preventive Medicine Initiative — Tanana Chiefs Conference proposes an integrated Lifestyle Medicine and Clinical Prevention model to strengthen prevention and improve early detection. The project addresses high burdens of chronic disease and cancer, low screening rates, and barriers to care across the TCC region. Built from within TCC in response to community-identified needs, the initiative redesigns preventive care delivery and expands access to lifestyle medicine grounded in locally tailored, community-driven approaches that reflect rural health priorities focused on prevention, wellness, and healthy communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Pharmaceutical and Medical Supplies Drone Transportation System For Interior Alaska Villages — Tanana Chiefs Conference proposes a concept formation and planning year to develop the regulatory, technical, and community engagement framework for a drone-based pharmaceutical delivery system connecting TCC's Fairbanks hub to 42 Interior Alaska villages across 94,000 square miles, where medication delivery delays of 5–14 days are common during winter. The project will partner with UAF's Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration (ACUASI) to address FAA BVLOS waiver requirements, chain-of-custody and DEA compliance, temperature maintenance, and tribal community readiness. Year 1 deliverables include a regulatory roadmap, safety and compliance framework, initial short-distance flight testing, and a 5-year phased implementation timeline.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Community Health Aide (CHA) and Behavioral Health Aide (BHA) Training Center — Tanana Chiefs Conference proposes to expand its Fairbanks CHA/P training center, with statewide tribal health partners, into a rural workforce training hub for Community Health Aides/Practitioners and Behavioral Health Aides, addressing limited training capacity, travel barriers, and workforce shortages in isolated Alaska communities through standards-aligned instruction, simulation, distance delivery, field-based learning, and trainee access planning.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Tuknisqat Ilat, Tuknisqat Acigtat (Strong Families, Strong Foundations) — Tangirnaq Native Village proposes establishing a culturally grounded family wellness, navigation, and prevention initiative that strengthens maternal and early childhood support, traditional healing, referral coordination, and community wellness infrastructure, addressing gaps in family engagement, service navigation, coordinated support, cultural connection, and prevention-focused resources for Alaska Native families across the Kodiak Archipelago through partnerships, family-centered programming, and community-based support systems.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: The Greater Fairbanks Community Hospital Foundation
data.programDescription: Team-Based, Value-Driven Primary Care Transformation in Interior Alaska — Foundation Health Partners proposes to transform the primary care system in Interior Alaska from an overburdened physician-centric fragmented, and reactive model to a patient-centered, coordinated, team based, technology enabled system that delivers timely, preventive, and continuous care for rural and frontier residents. The project will develop the clinic, IT, data and workforce infrastructure, and core competencies necessary for long-term participation in value-based care arrangements.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Rooted in Wellness: Building a Sustainable Model for Tribal Behavioral Health — The Central Council of Tlingit & Haida Indian Tribes of Alaska, through its 501(c)3 Tlingit & Haida Foundation (Foundation) proposes to build a sustainable Tribal behavioral health system for Southeast Alaska by expanding access to culturally grounded behavioral health services, developing a Tribal provider workforce pipeline, and establishing the billing, credentialing, and health information infrastructure needed to address workforce shortages, unmet behavioral health needs, and long-term service sustainability for Tribal citizens in rural and remote communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: TNR Technology Suite — True North Recovery proposes implementing a coordinated technology suite and upgraded data infrastructure, addressing fragmented communications and limited rural behavioral health access to expand telehealth-enabled substance use disorder and mental health services for isolated populations across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Wasilla Peer Crisis Residential Respite Center — True North Recovery proposes the Wasilla Peer Crisis Residential Respite Center to bridge a critical gap in the regional crisis continuum. Facing 45 opioid-related fatalities and responding to over 1200 mobile crisis calls, local data confirms an urgent need for subacute residential care. By expanding crisis services and leveraging current partnerships, this project offers a replicable, data-driven model for Alaska. This pilot establishes an actuarially sound, peer-led framework for sustainable, value-based care, that can be replicated across Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Alaska Graduate Medical Education (AKGME) Council:  Building Alaska's Rural Physician Workforce Infrastructure — The University of Alaska Anchorage, College of Health, Area Health Education Centers (AHEC) proposes establishing the Alaska Graduate Medical Education Council to coordinate physician residency training, support healthcare organizations in developing training programs, strengthen faculty and preceptor capacity, and assess physician workforce needs, addressing Alaska's shortage of residency training opportunities and physicians across rural, remote, frontier, and underserved communities statewide.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.awardeeName: University of Alaska Fairbanks - Community and Technical College
data.programDescription: Alaska Immersive Training Project — The University of Alaska Fairbanks Community and Technical College proposes to expand healthcare workforce training by deploying mobile and fixed immersive simulation systems serving rural Alaska. The project addresses limited access to clinical training caused by geographic isolation, low patient volumes, and shortages of specialty training opportunities. Immersive learning environments will provide realistic patient care scenarios and hands-on skills practice for emergency medical personnel, nurses, community health aides, and other healthcare workers in rural communities throughout Alaska.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Upstream Family Medicine OB Capacity Building Initiative — Upstream Family Medicine proposes recruiting a Family Medicine OB physician and providing advanced obstetric and newborn critical care training for current physicians, addressing obstetric workforce shortages and impending provider retirements across the Central Kenai Peninsula. The project will strengthen local rural capacity to provide prenatal, delivery, postpartum, and newborn care for families in the region.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Bridging Gaps and Expanding Access Through Community Pharmacy-Based Care for Remote Patients — Whale Tail Pharmacy proposes to establish eight community pharmacy-based health programs — including remote chronic disease monitoring, point-of-care testing, medication packaging, and transition of care support — to address the numerous healthcare needs and gaps in care on Prince of Wales Island, a roadless island in Southeast Alaska serving approximately 5,000 residents across 12 communities with no hospital, no home health nor long-term care, and limited physician access.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: After Hours Access to Pharmaceuticals — White's Inc proposes to purchase and install a Pharmaself24 medication cabinet at 106 Lincoln Street in Sitka to improve access to medication therapy for those unable to reach the pharmacy during normal operating hours. This will help to serve the population of Sitka and the surrounding local islands.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Grow Our Own: VR-Enabled K-12 Healthcare Certification Pipeline for Rural Alaska — Wrangell Public School District (WPSD) proposes implementing a virtual reality-based healthcare career education program for WPSD middle and high school students and across Southeast Alaska. The program addresses the lack of local advanced health science instructional expertise through immersive curriculum and comprehensive teacher professional development, providing foundational health science education needed to pursue certifications as CNAs, EMTs, BHA/Ps, CHA/Ps, DHATs, and CHWs, filling critical workforce roles that remain understaffed in remote Alaska communities.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Pathways for Alaska's Technical Healthcare Careers — Yukon Koyukuk School District proposes implementing dual healthcare career pathways in Certified Nurse Aide training and remote patient monitoring support to address healthcare workforce shortages, limited local care capacity, and growing telehealth needs in rural Alaska. The project serves high school students and healthcare partners across Yukon Koyukuk School District, YKSD partner school districts and communities, strengthening access to healthcare training and technology-enabled care support.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Deployment of Virtual Care Units to Expand Telehealth in Village Clinics — Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation proposes deploying low-bandwidth Virtual Care Units in village clinics to strengthen telehealth infrastructure and expand access to specialty, follow-up, and higher-acuity care for approximately 30,000 residents across the roadless, remote Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Healthcare Express: Increasing colonoscopy access to patients in remote locations — Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation proposes implementing a mobile colonoscopy service to expand access to colorectal cancer screening in subregional clinics across the Yukon-Kuskokwim region. This project addresses geographic and transportation barriers that currently require patients to fly to Bethel for routine colonoscopy care, contributing to missed appointments and delayed screening.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Modernizing Village Clinic Network Infrastructure to Support Telehealth and Cloud Systems — Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation proposes expanding its network infrastructure and capabilities to strengthen network connectivity and cybersecurity protection and enable more sophisticated technology platforms. This project will span across 48 village clinics, addressing aging systems that limit reliable connectivity, cybersecurity, telehealth, and cloud-based clinical tools in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Expanding Community Health Aide Training Capacity in the YK Region — Yukon-Kuskokwim Health Corporation proposes expanding the Community Health Aide Training (CHAT) program in Bethel to increase programs capacity and expand the regional healthcare workforce. The Community Health Aide Training Center in Bethel trains most of the Community Health Aides serving the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta and currently has a waitlist of 36-40 trainees for session one. Once trained, these community health aides provide routine, acute, and emergency direct patient care in village clinics.

sourceDocument.title: AK - 2026 - Alaska RHTP Year 1 Awards — $207.69M (Preliminary) Across 217 Projects Through Week 5

data.programDescription: Statewide Health Information Exchange Expansion — healthEconnect Alaska proposes to strengthen Alaska’s statewide health data infrastructure by expanding health information exchange connectivity and interoperability, particularly for small and rural healthcare providers. Key activities include supporting EMR interoperability standards, providing technical assistance and connectivity funding, expanding population health dashboards and claims-based analytics to support Pay For Value projects, and strengthening care coordination through real-time event notifications, care team visibility, and referral tools. These activities align with milestones identified in DOH’s RHTP application including 1) Expand statewide health information exchange; 2) Enter contracts to expand HIE interoperability; and 3) Provide targeted investments for participating in electronic health record systems.

data.awardeeName: Oregon Health Authority Announces Funding for Rural Hospitals and Rural Health Clinics The Oregon Health Authority (OHA), in partnership with the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) and the Office of Rural Health (ORH), is announcing funding for rural hospitals and Rural Health Clinics (RHCs) across Oregon. This funding is part of Oregon’s Rural Health Transformation Program, a multi-year effort to strengthen access to care and support health care delivery in rural communities across the state. All eligible RHCs will be offered a standardized funding amount. Rural hospitals will also be offered funding through a tiered approach , designed to reflect differences in size and capacity. Final funding amounts for year 1 are outlined below. Organizations Offered Funds Rural Hospitals Smaller Hospitals with less than or equal to 50 beds: The 32 rural hospitals with less than or equal to 50 beds are eligible for $ 963,000. data.programDescription: A predominantly Plain-community maternity population around Birth Care’s Gordonville (Harvest Drive) location travels by horse and buggy to reach care, and without on-site diagnostic, monitoring, and infusion capacity the rural site closest to these families cannot deliver locally the prenatal and postpartum care they depend on, so time-sensitive complications go unwatched and avoidable trips multiply. data.programDescription: The requested funding will support a coordinated set of high-impact projects that collectively improve safety, functionality, and long-term sustainability. A primary focus of the proposed funding is the modernization of patient care environments to meet current behavioral health safety and infection control standards. Upgrades to inpatient unit bathroom fixtures, including showers, toilets, and sinks across 32 patient rooms, will replace deteriorated infrastructure that currently requires frequent repair and presents ongoing infection control and safety challenges. These improvements are expected to reduce maintenance-related service calls in these areas by an estimated 30–40% and significantly decrease the likelihood of unplanned outages that could impact patient room availability. Additional safety enhancements include the replacement of standard shower curtains with behavioral health–appropriate soft magnetic doors designed to reduce ligature risk. This project directly aligns with current behavioral health design standards and is expected to eliminate a known environmental risk factor within 100% of affected patient bathing areas. The upgrade supports a safer care environment while reducing staff monitoring burden and enhancing patient dignity. Region: Northwest. Initiative: Tech & Infrastructure.

These supplies and euipment include an ultrasound machine to support both telehealth and in person Maternal Fetal Medicine specialty care. Teladoc TV Pro 300 carts that will allow the hospital to connect bedside patients with remote clinicians and have these visits integrated with the electronic medical record. Smart beds will replace beds across acute care units to prevent falls and improve patient outcomes. Five Retina Vue Scanners will provide retinal screening for more than 2605 patients with diabetes. Twelve Stryker Medical stretchers with 30” wheels, 700lbs capacity and a scale will allow for seamless transport through the Emergency Department as well assist with accurate vital signs. Region: Northeast. Initiative: Tech & Infrastructure.

data.programDescription: The project addresses substantial physical barriers that currently limit equitable access to behavioral health services at 905 Washington Street. Although portions of the building were renovated to support psychiatric and MAT treatment services, the facility currently lacks a fully ADA-compliant accessible route from designated parking areas into the treatment environment. Individuals with mobility limitations, chronic medical conditions, or physical disabilities face unnecessary barriers to independently accessing behavioral health treatment services. Program funding will support construction of an ADA-accessible route from designated handicapped parking spaces to the treatment facility through installation of a compliant exterior ramp system leading to an elevated deck area and direct building entry. The project also addresses a significant interior life-safety and patient access issue affecting second-floor clinical space currently utilized for behavioral health treatment. The existing interior stair system limits safe and efficient access to second-floor treatment areas due to inadequate pitch and spatial limitations. This creates challenges for patients, staff, and individuals with mobility concerns seeking behavioral health services upstairs. The project also addresses infrastructure conditions that threaten the long-term viability of behavioral health treatment space at the 905 Washington Street facility. Roof deterioration and water intrusion have affected portions of the building, including areas supporting existing behavioral health services. Without intervention, continued deterioration risks progressive damage to treatment space, increased maintenance costs, and potential reduction in usable licensed service capacity. Region: Southern Alleghenies. Initiative: Tech & Infrastructure.

data.programDescription: Nulton Diagnostic and Treatment Center, P.C. (NDTC) will implement a centralized technology platform designed to support Rapid Access Psychiatric Services and Community-Based Intensive Treatment (CBIT) across rural Pennsylvania, with initial deployment at its licensed location in Cambria County. The platform will enable real-time referral intake, scheduling, patient tracking, and performance monitoring, and consists of two integrated components: (1) a Rapid Access coordination module that allows referring providers, including emergency departments, crisis response systems, and inpatient psychiatric units, to schedule psychiatric appointments within one business day, and (2) a CBIT management and oversight module that supports providers and managed care organizations in monitoring adherence to the CBIT model and tracking utilization and performance. Region: Southern Alleghenies. Initiative: Tech & Infrastructure.

data.programDescription: Funding will support critical electrical infrastructure upgrades that are essential to the continued operation of healthcare services in a rural county without a hospital. WCHC is an electric-dependent facility housing 14 healthcare-related organizations that collectively supported approximately 46,000 patient visits in 2025. The project will replace major electrical distribution infrastructure serving the facility, including the main electrical switchboard “MDS,” distribution switchboards and motor control centers, and selected panelboards and transformers. These systems support the continued operation of healthcare providers, diagnostic services, emergency response functions, telecommunications and data systems, life-safety systems, elevators, environmental controls, and other building systems required to maintain safe and reliable access to care. Region: Northern Tier. Initiative: Tech & Infrastructure.
